correctness.rationale: All-order proof: uniqueness of incomparability-connected ordinal factors, width-two constraint reduces each to singleton or parallel pair of chains, exact strict degree formula, disjoint predecessor-count intervals, and a greedy inversion using the counts at predecessor prefix p. Equal degree pairs coincide with orbits because the only nontrivial factor automorphisms swap equal chains. The generating series counts unique normal forms. Complete canonical series/parallel enumeration through six points plus all vertex permutations proves first boundary at five points. Two independent Python implementations replayed: 7,232 width-two forms through order 12; all 238 canonical series-parallel forms through order 6. No unproved infinite inference from enumeration.

value.rationale: Motivation precedes calculation: predecessor/successor counts are the first one-dimensional counting-refinement observable in the strict-order language. A full normal form recovered from this coarse unlabeled signature is a structural isomorphism classification for an infinite natural forbidden-subposet class, with an explicit decoder and an enumerative formula. The sharp width-three five-vertex counterexample and exhaustive minimality certify exactly how the first-round orbit statement fails. This is a natural boundary, not an arbitrary small parameter slice, and does not require a downstream theorem.
